channel.title: The VFX Supervisor Daily
channel.description: What the day's VFX news means, in a few lines, with a link to every story.

item.title: #28: AI platforms aim at the full VFX pipeline, so bids may need an AI position
item.description:
An all-in-one AI filmmaking platform is pitching itself at work that independent VFX teams are usually hired for. Worth deciding now how your bids treat AI, before clients ask.

AI moves into the production pipeline

Tools are being sold as covering story, assets, VFX, editing and grade in one place, with logs of models, prompts and costs. That could shift what clients expect to pay for, and what they ask you to show. Worth having a clear stance on AI use, tracking and human review.

  • AI Filmmaking Platform Core Studio Launches at Taiwan Creative Content Fest With 24 Specialized Agents · variety.com Its VFX, grade and cost-tracking agents target work you might bid on, and the audit trail hints at what clients may want to see
  • Hollywood Has Flipped on GenAI, Says ‘Avatar’ VFX House Weta FX Chief: ‘If You Don’t Have an AI Strategy, Don’t Bother’ · imdb.com Clients will expect a stated AI strategy in bids

item.title: #27: Weta says studios now want a vendor AI plan before they will hire
item.description:
Weta's chief says big clients have moved from banning generative AI to expecting vendors to have a plan for it, which bears directly on how you pitch. Stage supply and incentive rules are shifting too, and those feed straight into bid budgets.

Update: incentives and market conditions

Update: the new items are about money in the budget. A proposed US federal credit and Hungary's lifted cap could change where shows are priced and shot. Treat both as inputs to scenario bids, not settled facts.

  • “Cautious” buyers head to AFM at critical time for independent sector · screendaily.com A proposed 20% transferable US credit, stackable with state incentives, could pass by early next year, so model it in US-shoot bids
  • Can Hungary rebuild film industry trust in the post-Orban era? · screendaily.com Hungary's cap on its 30% rebate was removed by July, so Budapest is again priceable after producers lost projects

Shows and who did the work

Breakdowns give you scope benchmarks for mid-size vendors and show how small houses win and credit work. Use them for team size, schedule and shot-count comparisons when you scope your own bids.

  • Neagley: WeFX Breaks Down Its Visual Effects Work · artofvfx.com About 70 artists for eight months on 250-plus shots is a usable benchmark for scoping episodic work
  • Roxel Creative Shares 'Backrooms' VFX Breakdown Reel · Animation World Network Roxel's supervisor also held the film's associate VFX supervisor credit, a pattern worth noting when you structure vendor roles
  • Stranger Things live-action prequel series set for Netflix in 2028 · c21media.net A 2028 Netflix prequel is far off and names no vendors, so it is a long-lead item to track

item.title: #26: Italy's reform and studio ownership moves reshape where and with whom to bid
item.description:
Italy has passed its film reform but left the tax credit details for later, so it is a watch item rather than a bidding lever.

Tax incentives and policy

Italy's reform promises easier permits and co-production rules, but no new credit rates yet. Those depend on decrees due within two years. Worth tracking if you pitch Italian shoots, but do not build a budget on it. Pact's note on UK employment rights is a compliance point for UK-based work.

  • Italy passes sweeping film and TV reform, with measures to attract international shoots · screendaily.com Italy's credit rates are unchanged for now, so treat it as a future option for incoming shoots and not a bid assumption
  • Pact Homepage · pact.co.uk New UK employer duties on union access and harassment are now in effect, which affects any UK company you run or hire through

Update: Weta FX and Taiwan

Update: Weta is investing in Taiwanese house Moonshine Studio and setting up a joint venture to bring local work up to international standard. It is still thin on pricing, so the question is whether Taiwan becomes a credible sub-vendor option.

  • Weta FX Partners With TAICCA To Position Taiwan As AI Hub; Invest In Moonshine Studio · uk.news.yahoo.com A named investment in Moonshine and a joint venture suggest a new Asian vendor option tied to Weta, though rates and capacity are not stated

Studio deals and ownership

Independent studios are finding ways to scale. 1920 VFX stays independently owned after a management buyout, with a Bangalore site opened in 2025. EightyEight Pictures and WildBrain have struck a CG production partnership, which could signal how animation studios share CG capacity, though the details are still worth watching. If you sub work out, expect more partners with India-based production arms.

  • ​1920 VFX completes founder-backed management buyout · shots.net A stable, investor-backed independent London vendor with a Bangalore site is a possible partner or benchmark for your own bids
  • WildBrain, EightyEight Pictures Strike CG Production Partnership · awn.com Shows a client outsourcing CG execution to an India-based vendor while keeping creative control in-house, a model you may be asked to match

Virtual production and new tools

Vancouver LED capacity is being rebuilt after Sony's Pixomondo closure, and Dark Slope is also launching a consulting arm for custom stage builds. That gives you another route to a volume in Canada. Training and tool items show where crew skills and pipelines are heading.

  • Dark Slope to Open New Virtual Production Stage in Vancouver (Exclusive) · hollywoodreporter.com A new Vancouver LED stage from December gives you a volume option in an incentive-rich market, plus a consultancy for custom builds
  • How to get more women working with virtual production in the Nordics? · nordiskfilmogtvfond.com Shows virtual production skills are being actively trained in the Nordics, which may widen the crew pool outside the usual hubs
  • fxguide · fxguide.com Headlines point to generative AI and Nuke plugin developments, worth a look for pipeline planning, though the excerpt gives no detail

Notable shows and who did the work

Vendor splits on recent shows are useful references for how work gets divided. Weta FX led Resident Evil and Moana with smaller specialists alongside, while Silverlake Studios was sole vendor on a 400-shot series.

  • The Pedestrian, Mutant Bryan and all the crazy creatures in Zach Cregger’s ‘Resident Evil’ · befores & afters Resident Evil's 708 shots were split across Weta FX, UPP, Wylie Co. and Lola, a template for a multi-vendor bid
  • fxpodcast: Wētā FX brings the ocean, lava and islands of Moana to life · fxguide Weta FX's 441 shots on Moana show how a lead vendor can take a defined chunk, such as the third act, of a larger show
  • The Drop: A Snowfall Saga – A Look at the VFX Created by Silverlake Studios · artofvfx.com A sole-vendor award of over 400 shots on a streaming series shows mid-size studios can win whole shows

item.title: #25: Tax credits are steering post and VFX work, so early planning decides who wins bids
item.description:
Geoff's take: It's nothing new that tax incentives have a big influence on where film work gets done, but a trend of producers working with VFX earlier in the process is welcomed.

Incentives are shaping where post and VFX money lands, from New York to the UK. Vendors who join projects early and offer several disciplines under one roof look best placed. Worth watching how that shapes the packages you bid into.

Incentives pull post capacity into place

Harbor's bigger New York base follows an extended state tax credit, which suggests incentives still steer where facilities invest. For a Copenhagen bidder, that may mean stronger US competition for multi-discipline post packages, and a reason to check which credits sit under any co-production.

  • Harbor Opens New Flagship Studios in New York, LBB · lbbonline.com A large multi-discipline New York facility, tied by the source to the credit's extension to 2037, may sharpen competition for US-linked post work
  • Harbor Opens Second New York City Post Studio in Hudson Square · postperspective.com Confirms the same opening and room count independently, and the credit link, so the expansion looks like a settled investment rather than a one-off claim

Early VFX involvement and indie co-production funding

The Loc Studios says UK credits are lifting independent features and that early input on recces and shoot planning gave its best results. That is a model worth copying in bids: sell supervision before the shoot. It is one UK studio's view, so treat it as a signal.

  • The Loc Studios expands into on-set VFX · televisual.com Shows a rival pitching early recce and planning input, and co-productions mixing UK, Canadian and Portuguese incentives, which may open doors for Nordic partners

Big shows and who delivered them

Credits and scale figures on tentpoles help benchmark crew size, hours and shot counts when pricing comparable work. They also show which vendors are winning visible sequences, useful when judging competitors and partners.

  • 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day': Sony Pictures Imageworks' Web-Tastic VFX · Animation World Network Gives usable benchmarks: 260 artists, over 101,000 hours and 449 shots, plus the simulation-heavy sequence the team called labour-intensive
  • The Bluff: El Ranchito Showcases Storm and Crocodile VFX · artofvfx.com El Ranchito's storm, ships and crocodile work is a reference for water and creature capability at a vendor you may meet in bids

Post planning at packaging stage

The piece argues producers should bring post in when packaging a project, to cut costs and ease casting. If it holds, it supports pushing for earlier VFX involvement in your own bids.

  • The rewards of putting post-production centre stage · c21media.net The teaser backs pitching post and VFX input at packaging stage, though without the full text the evidence is thin

item.title: #24: A French mocap stage seeks rescue while Weta FX bets on AI in Taiwan
item.description:

item.title: #23: California's bigger tax credit pitch adds to the pull on US-bound VFX work
item.description:
California wants to lift its film and TV credit to at least $1bn a year through 2040, yet shooting days keep falling. Competing incentive regimes are pulling work around, so Copenhagen bids should price in shifting budgets. Worth watching whether the federal proposal advances.

Tax incentives

A larger, longer California credit could pull more productions and their VFX budgets toward the US, and it adds to competition for work that might otherwise go to European vendors. Yet the credit rise last year did not stop the fall in shooting days, so the effect is uncertain. Worth tracking the federal bill too.

  • California governor proposes $1bn film and TV tax credit · screendaily.com A credit running to 2040 with a $100m independent slot may shift where producers place work, so watch for effects on your pitches
  • As Production Jobs Flee California, Governor Gavin Newsom Pushes to Expand Film and TV Tax Credit to $1 Billion Annually · indiewire.com It names the UK and Hungary as rival hubs, which suggests incentive competition will stay tight for any Danish bid

Virtual production pipeline

On-set image accuracy is being treated as a pipeline issue, not just a colour issue. If previews are trusted more, fewer look decisions may slip into post. That could affect how you scope on-set supervision and final-pixel risk in bids.

  • A Reliable Image From Virtual Production Through Color · tvtechnology.com It suggests virtual production teams want on-set looks closer to final, which may cut post surprises you would otherwise have to budget for

Crew and supervisors

Useful for benchmarking how a large-scale vendor structures its leadership when you scope your own team.

  • Resident Evil: Kevin Smith (VFX Supervisor), Jo Davison (Additional VFX Supervisor), Eric Reynolds (Animation Supervisor) and Janet Walters (VFX Producer) – Weta FX · artofvfx.com

item.title: #22: New stages and visualisation hubs open as AI pressure on crew grows
item.description:
Capacity is being added in places where work is thin, and AI is being sold as a way to cut crew. For a Copenhagen bidder, that suggests more rivals chasing the same shows at lower prices. Worth watching: who builds virtual production and previs capacity, and where.

New capacity, thin demand

Stages and previs hubs are opening while New Mexico spend is far below its peak. Incentive-backed regions with virtual production can undercut on price. Expect more places pitching the same shows, and check which of them can actually deliver.

  • Albuquerque film campus bets on virtual production to draw projects to state · abqjournal.com Shows a region using virtual production and local incentives to win shows back, a pitch that may compete with your bids
  • Albuquerque's The Lot Film Campus Opens on Former GE Site · hoodline.com Adds that the $50 million a year is only a target, so treat the campus as capacity, not proven work
  • PROOF RETURNS TO AUSTRALIA WITH NEW BRISBANE STUDIO · filmink.com.au Another visualisation player widening its reach to Asia-Pacific, which may mean more competition for previs and virtual production bids

AI and crew demand

One Thai executive expects crew demand to fall sharply and plans a hybrid film at half the usual budget. It is a single view, not a measured trend. Still, budgets like that could set clients' price expectations on bids.

  • AI set to slash demand for film crews · bangkokpost.com A claimed 40% crew cut and a halved budget target may shape client price expectations, though the forecast is one executive's view

item.title: #21: DNEG's Ramayana work shows how a single studio group can anchor an IMAX epic
item.description:
DNEG is working with sister company ReDefine on an IMAX two-parter, and Netflix is talking up AI at its Eyeline VFX arm. Both point to work consolidating inside large groups with in-house tools. Worth watching what that leaves for outside bidders.

Group-led VFX and in-house AI

Ramayana keeps a large share of its VFX inside the Prime Focus Group, with DNEG and ReDefine side by side. Netflix is also discussing AI at its own Eyeline studio. This suggests large owners may keep more work and tooling in-house, which could narrow openings for independent studios. Worth watching for subcontract or overflow work.

  • Inside Ramayana’s VFX universe: How DNEG is building a mythological world for global cinema · businesstoday.in Shots and DNEG's share are undisclosed, but sister-company teamwork suggests in-group work, so outside vendors should expect limited subcontract openings

item.title: #20: Nolan's single-vendor Odyssey and a pricey Potter series shape how to pitch
item.description:
The Odyssey kept its shot count under 500 by building monsters for real first, a model for lean bids. HBO's Harry Potter series budget suggests demand for creature and environment work. Worth watching how AI cost talk reaches clients.

Practical first, fewer shots

Practical-first plates kept The Odyssey's shot count low, yet the Cyclops still needed heavy augmentation. Bids for similar work should price plate clean-up and editorial prep, not just final shot count. Pipeline write-ups are also useful references for creature and compositing budgets.

  • Andrew Jackson & DNEG Embark on a Different Journey with 'The Odyssey' · Animation World Network Shows a sole-vendor DNEG job where a low shot count hid 260,000 frames of augmentation: price the prep, not just the count
  • Godzilla Minus Zero publishes its VFX breakdown and shows its pipeline · foro3d.com A pipeline breakdown on a kaiju made with limited resources is a usable reference for tight-budget creature bids
  • Moana: Weta FX Brings Te K? and Te Fiti to Life in the Epic Third Act · artofvfx.com Credits Weta FX with the prologue, storm and third act sequences on Moana, a guide to how big sequences get split

Update: Nuke Stage and the Mac

  • Foundry’s Nuke Stage now supports macOS · provideocoalition.com

AI and VFX costs

A cinematographer is publicly saying AI could cut VFX costs on big productions. It is one voice, not a trend, but clients may hear it. Expect questions on where machine learning can replace outsourced clean-up work.

  • Matthew Libatique Says AI Could Cut Marvel’s VFX Costs, but Doubts It Will Use AI Actors · mezha.net Libatique names glare correction as machine learning work that could replace cheap offshore labour, the sort of task you may be asked to reprice

Franchise money

HBO's Harry Potter series is reported to rank among its most expensive, per early estimates. If so, it may mean sustained creature, environment and virtual production work, with vendors competing early for key sequences.

  • HBO prepares a Harry Potter series with a record budget · foro3d.com A reportedly record-level series budget suggests creature and environment work, and early positioning for sequences may matter for bidding

item.title: #19: Breakdown reels show who wins lead-vendor work, while USD and incentives shift the ground
item.description:
Lead-vendor wins on big and mid-size shows set the benchmark you bid against, and some now openly use generative AI. Standards work on USD and a shaky freelance picture in the UK and California are the context to watch when pricing and staffing.

Shot breakdowns and show credits

Reels show who holds lead-vendor slots and at what scale: a 418-shot lead at one end, sole-vendor 300 to 380 shot packages at the other. Useful for calibrating your own bids. The BOT VFX note on generative AI beside CG suggests AI is entering delivered work.

  • Digital Domain Breaks Down 418 VFX Shots for Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day' · awn.com Sets a scale marker: a lead vendor with nearly 400 artists, plus a new creature muscle system that may raise the bar on creature bids
  • Lugundtrug breaks down the VFX of Der Medicus II with more than 380 shots · foro3d.com A German studio as sole VFX provider on 380-plus shots shows what a single European vendor can take on, relevant to Nordic and European competition
  • Young Washington: BOT VFX Recreates 18th-Century America with Invisible Effects · artofvfx.com BOT VFX credits generative AI alongside CG on 300-plus shots, a sign AI use is being openly stated in delivered work
  • Framestore Revisits the CG Joey and 300-Strong Cavalry of 'War Horse' · Animation World Network Mostly clean-up and replication rather than hero creature work, a reminder that much of a bid is invisible fixes, and that is worth pricing

Update: virtual production in Europe

Update: the new piece looks at Europe-wide LED stage growth, with Nordic pop-up stage use named. It also flags readiness gaps among smaller companies, which may limit VP demand and shape what clients ask you to quote.

  • Beyond the backlot: Reinventing drama in the age of virtual production · nordiskfilmogtvfond.com Nordic VP use is real but skills and cost barriers remain, so expect uneven client demand and tight planning requirements

USD standards in the pipeline

An open test bed is exposing where USD handling differs between tools, including renderers lighting the same asset differently. If you run or plan a USD pipeline, this is free validation material and an early warning on interchange problems with partner vendors.

  • Academy Software Foundation’s USD Working Group Launches USD Collaborative Projects Initiative · aswf.io Worth pulling into your own pipeline tests before relying on USD for cross-vendor asset handover

Update: incentives and freelance labour

Update: California is discussing lifting or removing its cap, though lawmakers call it a heavy lift. The UK Budget disappointed the freelancer union over tax timing. Both bear on where work goes and on freelancer cashflow and rates.

  • UK Budget ‘missed opportunity’ to help freelancers claims Bectu chief Childs · c21media.net Earlier tax payments could squeeze UK freelancers' cashflow, which may feed into rate demands if you hire from the UK

item.title: #18: AI is moving into Nuke and Resolve, so bid for new workflows
item.description:
Both main finishing tools now plug into AI assistants, which may shift how you scope compositing and post hours. Meanwhile UK studio money keeps flowing, and cross-border vendor ties are winning real shot counts. Worth checking pipeline assumptions before the next bid.

Studios and incentives

UK public money is backing new stage space outside London. More capacity could ease competition for stages and may widen where UK-based productions shoot, which matters if you bid against or alongside British vendors. The NSI lab headline hints at similar training investment elsewhere, but there is no detail to act on.

  • UK Budget promises £20 million for ‘Hollywood of the North’ · tvbeurope.com Two new sound stages in Liverpool, backed by £20 million, may add UK capacity and regional competition for shows you pitch for
  • NSI launches AI, virtual production lab in Manitoba · playbackonline.ca A Canadian AI and virtual production lab is a sign of public money going into these skills, though the headline alone gives no detail

AI in pipelines

Nuke and Resolve are both gaining AI hooks. Generative elements inside the comp graph and assistant-driven automation in post could trim routine hours, so your bids may need to say where AI is allowed and how it is priced. Nuke 18.0 is only in beta, so treat it as something to test.

  • Foundry releases Nuke 18.0 in open beta · cgchannel.com A Griptape node in Nuke lets compositors generate elements in the node graph, which may change how you scope cleanup and element work
  • How AI assistants are speeding up post production · tvbeurope.com Resolve's assistant support automates metadata, versioning and batch tasks, which suggests lower post hours for repetitive work, worth testing before pricing

Notable shows and credits

Invisible work like environment extensions and small digital fixes is a steady source of work on series. Seeing how a vendor presents it shows what producers value in a showreel for this kind of job.

  • Lanterns: Discover CoSA VFX’s Invisible Effects, From Digital Landscapes to a Beard · artofvfx.com CoSA VFX's Lanterns work shows subtle environment extension is credited work worth pitching, and who to watch for similar series bids

Vendor partnerships

An Indian studio won 300 shots on a feature through a regional producer relationship built on trust. It suggests overflow work can go to well-connected partners, which is worth knowing when you weigh outsourcing or compete with it.

  • Beyond the Render: Craft, Hospitality and the Human side of Cross-Border VFX, LBB · lbbonline.com Resonance landing 300 shots on Land of Bad via a regional bridge shows the kind of offshore competition you may face on bids

item.title: #17: French VFX pay and AI rules are contested, while ILM spreads work across three sites
item.description:
French animation and VFX workers are pressing on pay, job titles and generative AI rules, which could shape costs and contract terms on shared European bids. Show breakdowns also show who is winning work and how it is split across sites. Worth watching: the 18 November walkout.

Labour action in France

The SNTPCT union has called a two-hour walkout of French animation and VFX workers, which could signal rising labour tension in the sector and is worth watching. If employers concede, French cost bases and AI clauses may shift. Worth watching for anyone pricing co-productions or subcontracting to French studios.

  • SNTPCT Calls for 2-Hour Walkout of French Animation and VFX Workers · Animation World Network Pay, job-title and AI demands could raise French labour costs and set a template for AI consent and credit clauses in bids

Pipeline tools

A Foundry video covers Katana, Nuke and USD use on Toy Story 5. It is a pointer to how a large studio builds its pipeline around USD.

  • New Foundry video looks at use of Katana, Nuke, and USD by Pixar in ‘Toy Story 5’ · befores & afters

ILM's dinosaur work

ILM delivered around 700 shots across Sydney, San Francisco and Vancouver, with environments in Sydney and previs, postvis and creatures elsewhere. That split suggests how large work is divided by site specialism. Useful reference when pitching environment-heavy or creature-heavy packages.

  • ILM Builds 700 Shots of Prehistoric Suburbia for 'The End of Oak Street' · Animation World Network Shows a clear site-by-discipline split on a 700-shot job, a model for structuring multi-site bids
  • ILM BRINGS DINOSAURS TO SUBURBIA FOR THE END OF OAK STREET · vfxvoice.com Production VFX supervisor Jay Cooper describes creature design freedom and digital geography fixes, useful for scoping similar creature and environment work

Who did the work on recent shows

item.description:

AI tools aimed at control and dialogue changes

Both items pitch AI as something that keeps human-made inputs in charge: 3D data guiding generation, and original performances preserved in lipsync. That may shift some cleanup and localisation work to managed services. Worth checking what your pipeline offers around consistency and ownership.

Netflix cuts and a tax-cap warning

item.title: #7: A new studio landing a horror feature shows where mid-size work is going
item.description:

Small studios taking on feature-scale work
